## Berlin 12-Month Lease Review

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

Here’s a practical pre-signing checklist tailored to a **2-bedroom Berlin apartment** with **€1,650 warm rent**, **68 m²**, **built 1998**, **8th floor**, **elevator**, and a requested **3-month cold-rent deposit**. I’m assuming a standard private residential lease in Germany.

## Lease Terms, Utilities, Deposit Checks

| Area | What to verify | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Rent type | Confirm **cold rent** vs **warm rent** and what is included | Warm rent can still exclude power, internet, and sometimes heating overages |
| Rent breakdown | Ask for the exact split: cold rent, operating costs, heating/hot water, any extras | Helps avoid surprise charges and makes future increases easier to check |
| Lease length | Confirm it is truly **12 months**, whether it auto-renews, and how notice works | Fixed-term leases in Germany need a valid reason in many cases |
| Notice period | Check the tenant notice period and any landlord termination rights | Important if you may leave early |
| Deposit | Verify the deposit is **max 3 months’ cold rent** and held separately | In Germany, deposit handling is tightly regulated |
| Deposit payment | Check if it can be paid in **3 monthly installments** instead of all at once | Tenants often have this right |
| Utilities | Confirm who pays **electricity, internet, GEZ/radio fee, and any meter-based costs** | These are often not included in warm rent |
| Repairs | Clarify responsibility for minor repairs, appliance issues, and wear-and-tear | Prevents disputes later |
| Building costs | Review what is included in **Nebenkosten** and whether recent bills are available | Operating costs can rise sharply |
| Apartment condition | Document walls, floors, windows, bathroom, kitchen, and appliances in the handover protocol | Protects your deposit when moving out |
| Noise/comfort | Check street noise, insulation, elevator reliability, and heating performance | Especially important on the 8th floor |
| Subletting/changes | Confirm rules for subletting, pets, drilling, and renovation | Useful if your plans change |
| Registration | Make sure you will receive the **Wohnungsgeberbestätigung** | Needed for Anmeldung in Berlin |

## Red Flags and Berlin-Specific Watchouts

- **Deposit above 3 months’ cold rent**: that is a major warning sign.
- **Deposit demanded in full immediately**: ask to pay in 3 installments if needed.
- **“Warm rent” with unclear inclusions**: always get a written breakdown.
- **Missing handover protocol**: do not skip a signed **Übergabeprotokoll** with photos.
- **No written permit for fixed term**: a time-limited lease should have a lawful reason.
- **Unclear operating costs**: ask for the latest **Nebenkostenabrechnung** or estimate.
- **Cash-only payment requests**: insist on traceable bank transfer.
- **Pressure to sign quickly**: take time to read every clause, especially termination and deposit terms.
- **Unlisted defects**: test windows, heating, water pressure, elevator access, and any built-in appliances before signing.
- **Unclear responsibility for repairs**: especially for kitchen appliances, radiators, and bathroom fixtures.
